messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

# Pricing

Every plan reviews every pull request. What changes is how much of your history the reviewer gets to read — and who you can call when it's wrong.

**Solo — free**
One private repo, unlimited public ones. Reviews land as a comment within about 90 seconds of a push. You get the same checks the paid plans get: logic errors, unhandled cases, the function someone already wrote in a different file two weeks ago. No card.

**Team — $18 per contributing seat / month**
Unlimited repos. The reviewer reads your last 12 months of merged PRs and learns what your team actually rejects, so it stops re-arguing the parameter order you settled in March. Owners get a ruleset file, per-directory severity, and a Friday digest of what slipped through. Seats are counted by who pushed code that month, so a dormant account costs you nothing. Email support, two business days.

**Enterprise — from $12,000/year**
Runs in your VPC or on your own hardware; the code never leaves. SAML, SCIM, audit logs piped to your SIEM. You get a named engineer, a four-hour response window, and a quarterly session where we tune the rules against your last 500 reviews. Volume pricing opens at 200 seats.

Annual billing takes 15% off Team. Nonprofits and classrooms pay nothing on either plan — just email us.

---

Swap in your product name and real numbers; the prices, SLA, and the "reads 12 months of merged PRs" claim are placeholders I invented to give the copy something concrete to stand on.
